   STAFF REPORT

 Meeting Date:  June 11, 2024
 To:  Arts and Culture Council Liaisons Councilmembers John Mirisch and
  Mary Wells
 From:  Matthew Brown, Recreation Services Manager
  Corrina Lesser, Recreation Supervisor
 Subject:  Festival Beverly Hills

 Attachments:  06-03-24 Arts and Culture Council Liaison Staff Report

INTRODUCTION
At the June 3, 2024 Arts and Culture Council Liaison meeting Community Services staff
and Arts and Culture Commission presented an event planning update for the 2024
Festival Beverly Hills.
At this meeting staff shared confirmed details of the event such as the date, Sunday July
21, 2024, and the event time 12:00pm – 6:00pm. Staff provided a number of additional
event details, identifying the means by which the event programming aimed to accomplish
the established goals of building on the success of the inaugural festival, and continuing
to establish Festival Beverly Hills as a cultural destination for both Beverly Hills and the
Greater Southern California region.
Through the continued collaborative efforts of staff and the Arts and Culture Commission
Performing Arts and Events Ad Hoc, staff highlighted the 2024 Festival Beverly Hills event
programming and marketing strategy, confirmed partnerships, and ways the festival would
showcase a diverse array of cultures. Some of the articulated goals for the 2024 Festival
Beverly Hills, as articulated through Ad Hoc meetings, were to engage more of our Los
Angeles area consular corps for participation, secure artists and festival elements,
representative of the diversity within Beverly Hills and the Greater Southern California
region, and include pop-up dance performances, and elements of engaging spectacle.
Some of the plans detailed for the 2024 Festival Beverly Hills included:
  •  Two performance stages, and multiple smaller areas of festival activation
  •  Representation from a wide range of cultures and consulates
  •  A diverse range of musical and dance performances, including both professional
  and cultural dance companies
  •  Global DJ sets, poetry, and puppeteering performances
 Meeting Date: June 3, 2024
  •  Record and book fair pop-up
  •  Food truck hubs with multiple dining and picnic areas
  •  A robust marketing plan was shared, including event postcards, event signage,
  digital advertising, social media campaigns, and more

The costs for 2024 Festival Beverly Hills, as planned at Roxbury Park, comes out to
$47,000, fits within the allocated event budget, and can be absorbed within the Community
Services budget. The Arts and Culture Commission Performing Arts and Annual Events
Ad Hoc Committee has identified additional talent that could be secured if additional
funding was provided. Notable artists that could potentially be added to the festival lineup
have been identified, and range in cost from approximately $5,000 - $15,000, Staff
requested direction from Council Liaisons on whether they would like to see any additional
type of festival programming, and if so, what the corresponding level of additional funding
they would support in a request to the full City Council.

DISCUSSION
At the June 3, 2024, Arts and Culture Council Liaison meeting Council Liaisons expressed
concerns about the intended Roxbury Park location for Festival Beverly Hills, and the
ability to attract adequate crowds at that location during the summer months, often popular
for travel, and without school in session. Alternate sites for Festival Beverly Hills were then
suggested as options, to place the festival closer to areas within Beverly Hills more
frequently visited by tourists and visitors, and near sites more famous and iconically
known.

Council Liaisons preferred that some additional festival locations be explored, that would
locate the festival closer to the visitor core of Beverly Hills, and sites that would more easily
draw upon visitors and tourists in addition to residents. Two additional locations were
suggested, including Beverly Gardens Park, and the block of Crescent Drive between
North Santa Monica Boulevard and South Santa Monica Boulevard, in front of the City
Hall campus. Council Liaisons identified that both locations would accomplish bringing the
festival closer to the visitor core and help associate Festival Beverly Hills with more of the
iconic symbols of Beverly Hills. Based on their request to bring forward information
associated with moving to one of the suggested locations, staff has worked to identify the
feasibility, and positive and negative impacts, associated with relocating Festival Beverly
Hills to either Beverly Gardens Park, or on Crescent Drive.

Beverly Gardens Park:
  • Event costs relocating Festival Beverly Hills to Beverly Gardens Park:
  o Event production costs would increase by $18,000 to $65,000
  o Beverly Gardens Park event location will incur additional event
  rental infrastructure costs, including dining, additional tenting for
  artists, and portable restrooms.
  o Estimated street closure costs 6am – 10pm: would be $9,000

  •  Benefits relocating Festival Beverly Hills to Beverly Gardens Park:
  o Sizeable and flexible event location, with the ability to grow or reshape the
  footprint in future years if desired
  o Destination for other Arts & Culture signature programs like the established
  bi-annual Art Show
  o Increased potential for organic visitor engagement due to the location's
  high visibility and iconic location
Page 2 of 4
 Meeting Date: June 3, 2024
  o  Shade and picnic opportunities that will encourage attendees to stay longer
  at the event
  o  Well known event space: institutional knowledge and experience producing
  large-scale, multi-faceted events in the park
  o  Maximum flexibility on event set-up
  o  Road closures managed by City staff

  •  Challenges relocating Festival Beverly Hills to Beverly Gardens Park:
  o No built-in on-site green room for artists
  o Increased vendor needs for restrooms, picnic tables, tenting, and other
  Festival infrastructure
  o Traffic/neighborhood impacts due to road closures

Crescent Drive/City Hall:
  • Event costs relocating Festival Beverly Hills to Crescent Drive/City Hall:
  o Event production costs would increase by $23,000 to $70,000
  o Crescent Drive event location will incur additional event rental infrastructure
  costs, including dining, additional tenting for artists, and portable
  restrooms.
  o Estimated street closure costs 6am-10pm would be $15,000

  •  Benefits relocating Festival Beverly Hills to Crescent Drive/City Hall:
  o Increased potential for organic visitor engagement due to the location's
  high visibility
  o City Hall is a striking visually iconic backdrop for the main stage
  o On-site artist’s green room

  •  Challenges relocating Festival Beverly Hills to Crescent Drive/City Hall:
  o Relatively fixed event footprint, with less ability to grow or reshape the
  footprint in years to come if desired
  o Increased vendor/partner needs including
  ▪ Restrooms, picnic tables, tenting, and other Festival
  infrastructure
  ▪ Road closure (use of vendor required to close Crescent)
  ▪ Likely need to extend the festival space (for example, utilizing
  the Wallis Anenberg motor court to provide a space further from
  the main stages, for the Storytelling Hub, and record and book
  fair pop-ups).
  o Minimal shade and picnic options which may limit or shorten audience
  attendance
  o Traffic/neighborhood impacts due to road closure  Commented [SH1]: We can remove this. You have identified

costs, and event planning considerations, if there is a desire to relocate Festival Beverly  Commented [MB2R1]: That is correct. Will include the

Boulevard and South Santa Monica Boulevard.

The costs to relocate Festival Beverly Hills in Beverly Gardens Park are projected to total
$65,000 including the estimated costs associated with street closures. Similar to the Art
Show, albeit on a much smaller scale, Festival Beverly Hills at Beverly Gardens Park
would necessitate some level of street closures along Canon between North Santa Monica
Boulevard and Park Way, and along Park Way. Street closures for the Beverly Gardens
location, would not necessitate the utilization of an outside vendor and can be done
working with Public Works and the Beverly Hills Police Department.
Page 3 of 4
 Meeting Date: June 3, 2024

The costs to relocate Festival Beverly Hills along Crescent Drive and adjacent City Hall
are projected to total $70,000 including the cost associated with street closures. This
location would necessitate the closure of Crescent Drive between North and South Santa
Monica Boulevard and use a contractual vendor to facilitate the street closure.

FISCAL IMPACT
The costs for the currently planned 2024 Festival Beverly Hills at Roxbury Park equate to
$47,000 and are allocated within the current Community Services Department operating
budget. To support the costs of either relocating Festival Beverly Hills to Beverly Gardens
Park, or on Crescent Drive and adjacent City Hall, an appropriation of additional funding
will be required.

 Proposed Site  Event Cost  Appropriation needed
 Beverly Gardens Park  $65,000  $18,000
 Crescent Drive/City Hall  $70,000  $23,000

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends based on the projected costs, the greater flexibility to program and
utilize Beverly Gardens as an event space now and moving forward, prior event site
experiences, and for the overall festival-goer experience, if Festival Beverly Hills is to
relocate, the recommendation is to relocate to Beverly Gardens Park. If there is a desire
to relocate Festival Beverly Hills to Beverly Gardens Park or along Crescent Drive this
year, or in the future, additional funding will need to be approved by the full City Council,
and at the level of associated costs outlined in this report.

Staff is seeking direction from the City Council Arts and Culture Council Liaisons on a
revised location for the 2024 Festival Beverly Hills.

  Stephanie Harris,
  Director of Community Services

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  June 11, 2024 / 1:00 PM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Councilmember John Mirisch, Councilmember Mary Wells, City Manager
  Nancy Coffey, Recreational Services Manager Matthew Brown, Director of
  Community Services Stephanie Harris, Arts and Culture Commission Vice
  Chair Karla Gordy Bristol

  1) Public Comment:

  None

  2) Festival Beverly Hills:
  a. Presentation by Matthew Brown:
  i. At the January 30th, 2024, Liaison meeting, the 2024 Festival Beverly Hills
  was moved to July 21st, 2024, and proposed to move to Roxbury Park.
  ii. At the June 3rd meeting, liaisons requested staff move the event to either
  Beverly Gardens Park or 400 N Crescent to better draw tourists to the
  event.
  iii. A Beverly Gardens event is projected to cost $65,000, which is $18,000
  more than Roxbury. Benefits would be that it’s a highly visible and flexible
  space that would draw in people and will allow for the event to easily
  expand in the future. The city also has a lot of experience with running
  events at the site. Some problems for the space include the lack of onsite
  festival infrastructure, which will need to be brought in, as well as
  neighborhood and community impacts due to road closures.
  iv. A 400 N Crescent event would cost $70,000, which is $23,000 more than
  Roxbury. Benefits include a highly visible space that will draw in people as
  well as onsite space for artists. Some problems include that the space is
  less flexible, lack of onsite festival infrastructure, which will need to be
  brought in, limited onsite shade, and neighborhood impacts due to road
  closures.
  b. Most of the cost increases from the 2023 to the Roxbury 2024 event were from
  bringing in infrastructure as well as the increased number of performances.
  c. Councilmembers Mirisch and Wells support moving the festival to Beverly Gardens
  Park.
